addendum.length_note: a focused addendum, not a second framework: it fixes the causal order, the exception boundaries, the inventory and the transitions of the items the review named

D1.defect: the barrier wait was placed immediately after session.start(), i.e. BEFORE the live worker/generation registration and BEFORE bind_deadline/clock.advance that actually trigger the cancellation at T10:4122-4145; the barrier could not announce itself there, and a late snapshot must not appear completed
D1.resolution: the barrier_entered event and that wait are WITHDRAWN. The original causal trigger is preserved and never moved: S1 session.start -> S2 bounded wait for read_waiting -> S3/S4 the live worker and the exact generation -> S5 bind_deadline + clock.advance (the actual cause) -> S6 inside the seam: the predicates, barrier['left_at'], the seam persists api.barrier_snapshot and sets api.barrier_completed -> S7 the phase waits (bounded 15 s) for barrier_completed -> S8 the durable barrier document is written FROM the persisted snapshot -> S9 the assertions read the persisted snapshot
rules: the event is barrier_completed, set by the seam at the finalization of the barrier; there is no entered event and no wait before S5
the snapshot is persisted by the seam; the phase never re-reads the live api.barrier, so a late snapshot can never look completed
a timeout of S7 persists an explicit premise failure {'status':'FAIL','premise':'BARRIER_NOT_COMPLETED','timeout_seconds':15.0,'barrier_completed':False} and the phase fails
expect_barrier='NOT_APPLICABLE' writes the document immediately with the empty snapshot and asserts barrier_snapshot['entered_at'] is None; no wait is performed there
the failure path keeps the barrier facts (T10:4304-4306) and adds barrier_completed and the snapshot

D2.defect: _chain was still outside the try, phase-construction was neither in the complete inventory nor covered by except/finally, the phase result was not distinguished from the individual check documents, the main schedule could become terminal PASSED before both stop oracles and the cleanup, and the earlier R10 work was outside the whole-test guard
D2.resolution: (a) the construction moved inside the local try with the holders initialised to None before it and the teardown skipping a None holder; (b) the inventory now holds five names per schedule (<phase> result, -construction, -barrier, -first, -second) plus the three published-before-timeout names plus r10-first/r10-second/r10-coordination = 31 names, all planned at the top of the test; (c) the phase RESULT document is separate from the CHECK documents, is written LAST after both stops and the cleanup, and is PASSED only when the barrier check, both stop checks and the cleanup all passed - a later failed stop makes the result FAIL while the earlier checks keep PASSED and their facts; (d) the whole-test guard covers the earlier R10 real-chain work, the coordination block and the five later schedules, and the finally writes NOT_RUN only for the names still PLANNED

D3.defect: pending_starts()==0 alone does not prove that no start follows the snapshot; the registry scope, the exact thread objects, the arming window and the overall bound of the resnapshots were undefined
D3.resolution: (a) one registry per round lifetime and the seam armed from before start_round until after that round's salvage (main round, zero round, each controlled subcase), so the seam stays armed through the product's stop and the late closer work; (b) the registration is keyed by id(thread) - the exact object - the name is only a label, the seam forwards every start it does not own, and a name match alone never claims ownership; (c) the seam observes only: it never blocks, refuses, reorders or delays a start and never touches a deadline, so no production decision is frozen; (d) the salvage of a round is a bounded drain loop with ONE overall bound of 30 s per round (the per-owner wait is cropped by the remaining budget and the budget is never reset), the quiescence assertion comes AFTER the drain and never before it, an unquiet round is a FAIL/UNKNOWN while the gates are still released and all the registered owners are still attempted, and if the bound is reached the proof fails truthfully with the last snapshot and the last salvage recorded; (e) the producers are the pump, the heartbeat, the closer, the channel drain and the two endpoint workers

D4.defect: 'controlled_close_failure in detail' is a substring test and not an exact token; the close case claimed that all deliberate errors unwind while it also records/catches the close exception inside the finally; the outer propagation/catch ordering was not spelled out; the original exception was not preserved
D4.resolution: (a) the substring test is WITHDRAWN: exactly one recorded failure, owner == 'controlled:transport', type == 'RuntimeError' (the exact class), detail == 'controlled_close_failure' (the exact message), and no record with another owner or another type; child_close_failures must be empty in every checkpoint, so an unrelated close or endpoint error fails the subcase; (b) the exact order is spelled out: the deliberate failure is raised inside the region -> the region runs every cleanup action in a fixed order (gates, transport close, each endpoint close, _capture_stop, the owner enumeration, the drain and salvage, the proof, the document) -> the region records every additional error and raises AssertionError(proof) only when no original failure is unwinding -> the original failure leaves the region and is caught by the outer except AFTER every other cleanup action was attempted -> the outer except records the exact type and token; CLOSE_FAILURE is explicitly NOT an unwinding case (its failure is produced by the cleanup itself, is recorded with its exact type and message, and the region continues with every other action); no expected sentinel is caught before the cleanup region; (c) the original failure is preserved and an additional error makes the overall proof fail

D5.defect: the _owner_start_state call was outside the salvage try, only a single error was kept, a classification failure aborted the remaining joins, KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit were not preserved, and _capture_stop did not save the actual full session evidence/state/retained resources
D5.resolution: (a) the classification moved inside the per-owner guard; every owner is attempted whatever fails; every error is retained in a LIST with its kind, exact type and detail (STATE / JOIN / LIVENESS), never a single first error and never a silent UNKNOWN without a diagnostic; the display name and the identity id(thread) are separate fields; (b) an interruption is recorded with its identity, re-raised at the end of the region when nothing else unwinds, and preserved as an additional error otherwise, and the region never reports a successful cleanup on an error; (c) _capture_stop names the REAL keys of the evidence DTO - including background_threads, which IS a valid key at C:2399-2406 (the root's factual correction: the earlier absent-field example was wrong and is not used) - keeps the object identities (session.broker is ..., id(session.broker)) apart from the display JSON, never hides a valid key behind a .get(), and records an explicit snapshot_error when the snapshot fails; the capture is taken before the salvage and on both paths
D5.root_factual_correction_applied: background_threads is a valid evidence key; the design keeps it and invents no field

design_answer.M1-a: C1 - patch.object(broker_module.BrokerProcess, 'read', zero_gated_broker_read): the class is the target and the replacement is the third positional argument (new), instead of assigning the string 'read' to the module attribute BrokerProcess.
design_answer.M1-b: C2 - the actual error value (pump.error is None, type name) is stored separately from the display repr(pump.error); the premise asserts the actual value.
design_answer.M1-c: C3/C4 - start_round returns the ACTUAL return value of the public NativeCustodySession.start and the zero round uses that captured return as the returned state of the product.
design_answer.M1-d: C5 - the retention oracle checks the VALUE (broker_retained is True), the IDENTITY (session.broker is the object of the round) and the original-handle identity source of the returned evidence, never the presence of the key.
design_answer.M1-e: C6/C7 - one ordered trace E1..E7 (start, pump read entered, reply wait entered/returned, gate released, queue get entered, pump ended) with the required order E1<E2<E3<E4<E5<E6<E7 and seven bounded checked no-EOF/timeout facts N1..N7.

design_answer.M2-a: C12 - the complete document list and the ledger are installed at the very top of test_n10_r10, before any setup and before any earlier r10 assertion, and the whole body is guarded.
design_answer.M2-b: C8/C10/C11/C12 - ledger.attempt(name) is called before every construction, every phase body and every stop.
design_answer.M2-c: C10a/C11 - a bounded wait on a new barrier_entered event, then the durable barrier document is written BEFORE the first assertion that depends on the barrier; the barrier facts of the failure path are kept.
design_answer.M2-d: C9/C10/C11/C12 - the failure handler rewrites every ATTEMPTED document as FAIL with the raw facts; a PASSED document is terminal and is never rewritten.
design_answer.M2-e: C10/C11 - the two real stops are marked ATTEMPTED before the call, so an attempted stop that raises is FAIL and never NOT_RUN.
design_answer.M2-f: C9 - record() persists first and marks the name written/attempted only after the write succeeded.
design_answer.M2-g: C12/C13 - the inventory never overwrites a written document, a NOT_RUN document carries no fact of a phase that was not established, and the original failure is never replaced.

M2.revision: REVISED by design.md section 10 (root review D1, D2, D5, D6): the barrier wait may no longer precede its cause (10.1), the construction is inside the local guard with None holders, the inventory is complete at 31 names, the phase RESULT is separate from the CHECK documents and is written last, and the whole-test guard covers the earlier R10 work and all later schedules (10.2, 10.6).

design_answer.M3-a: C14 - the cleanup region moves one nesting level outward and encloses start_round AND the RUNNING assertion.
design_answer.M3-b: C14/C15 - the deliberate sentinel, ordinary assertion and constructor failures are RAISED inside the cleanup region and CAUGHT outside it; the region records cleanup_ran_while_unwinding as a fact.
design_answer.M3-c: C16 - the seam calls the ORIGINAL threading.Thread.start (the thread really takes effect) and raises _R07ConstructorFailure inside the constructor, not after the constructor returned.
design_answer.M3-d: C16/C17 - the start seam forwards the original start and the original result, is scoped by the production thread name and by an armed flag, and the partial channel custody of B:5266-5267 is retained through the fixture custody.
design_answer.M3-e: C17 - the immediate start registration (STARTING before the original start, STARTED after it returned) plus the quiescence condition pending_starts() == 0 asserted before the final owner snapshot.
design_answer.M3-f: C20 - _capture_stop records the exception AND the live state, the retention and the retained broker identity of that moment, before the salvage; the product deadline is never renewed by the fixture.
design_answer.M3-g: C18 - every owner is attempted even when join or is_alive fails; the error is retained in the facts, alive becomes None and the proof fails; the salvage is bounded (10 s per owner, 30 s total).
design_answer.M3-h: C19 - NEVER_STARTED only with proven provenance from the registry, otherwise UNKNOWN, which fails the proof.
design_answer.M3-i: C21 - the fallback calls of _registry_owners pass the object first and the name second.
design_answer.M3-j: C15/C22 - the exact type and the exact token per checkpoint, and the close oracle rejects any unrelated close/endpoint failure.

M3.revision: REVISED by design.md section 10 (root review D3, D4, D5): the ownership scope per round lifetime, the registration of the exact thread object, the seam armed through the stop and the late closer, and the bounded drain with ONE overall 30 s bound whose quiescence assertion follows the drain (10.3); the exact close token, the exact per-checkpoint propagation/catch order and the preservation of the original failure (10.4); the classification inside the per-owner guard, the complete error lists, the preservation of KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit and the real evidence keys of _capture_stop including background_threads (10.5).
